next_question: This packet's own frozen design contains the contradiction that matters, and it is a design defect rather than a null result: the ONLY never-observed collection in the test set ('widgets') is scored as a semantic false-accept every time it is bound, so the frozen semantic-guard metric is maximized by a binder that abstains on every collection it has not seen, and there is no task anywhere in the 10000 raw rows in which binding an unobserved collection is the correct answer. The packet therefore measures REFUSAL, not the TRANSFER that C-PARAM-INHERIT's registry next_gate demands ('learn on resource A, succeed on never-observed B'). The next question: on this same proven substrate class, which is one of only two that have actually produced valid measurement in the program and needs no Docker, browser, model key or external site, CAN ANY SLOT-BINDER SATISFY BOTH OBLIGATIONS AT ONCE -- binding a collection that appears in ZERO training observations at a rate that beats the declared-vocabulary incumbent and the three structural nulls, WHILE holding the semantic false-accept at or below 0.10 on a well-formed identifier that is unjustifiable for the requested collection (a well-formed sibling of a different collection requested inside a seen one, where binding is REQUIRED and the sibling is wrong) -- with (i) an IDENTIFIER-LEVEL rather than collection-level support model compared head to head (closed set over observed collection values; shape and prefix family over identifier values; cross-collection prefix transfer; explicit no-evidence UNKNOWN), each scored on the unseen-collection binding rate AND the sibling-identifier false-accept rate SIMULTANEOUSLY so neither can be bought by refusing, with family-blocked, site-grouped uncertainty and non-degenerate interval width obtained by widening the identifier distribution rather than by adding arms; (ii) an explicit measurement of whether the incumbent's 1.0 rate of executing well-formed identifiers of an unobserved collection persists when the collection is SEEN and the identifier is a well-formed sibling of another collection, which is the residual risk a collection-level closed set does not cover and which no row in this packet tests, since every recorded abstention reason concerns slot s0; (iii) the abstention rate treated as a DESIGN PARAMETER AND A COST rather than a benefit, with the break-even against within-episode reuse and against retrieval-K5 re-reported at a product-plausible near-zero out-of-support request rate as well as at the frozen 50 percent, and with the induction budget reconciled between prereg 4.2 and 4.3 BEFORE any break-even is read; and (iv) as preconditions, the frozen decision rule repaired so the degeneracy guard cannot fire on a treatment arm or on a construction-perfect baseline and so F1-F4 are evaluated before it, the A4 tie rule fixed or the Frame-R primary designation swapped for Frame B with the non-discrimination documented, and freeze extended to bind a code hash so F8 is evaluable. Either outcome changes product architecture: a support model that admits unseen collections without admitting unjustifiable siblings is the induction principle C-PARAM-INHERIT, C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE and C-CROSSSITE all stand on, and a demonstration that no such model exists on this substrate is a bounded architectural negative that closes a design, not the search domain.
